newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares hit seventh consequtive record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares hit seventh consequtive record.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed an average 0.72 percent in late buying fuelled by positive Treasury-bill auction results on Tuesday, but trade was quiet due to lower turnover, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed at a seventh consequtive all-time high of 92,797.71, up 663.50 points from Monday's previous record of 92,134.21. Gains totalled 1.13 percent in two days after last week's 5.49 percent surge.
In dollar terms, the index was at $0.90, unchanged since Friday and compared to a record of $1 on April 8 and $0.67 at end-1995.
Trade volume dropped to 17.61 trillion lira ($170.4 million) from Monday's 18.54 trillion ($180.9 million).
The Treasury sold 100 billion lira nominal-valued 273-day bills, slashing the yield to 136.32 percent from 144.92 percent in the previous 182-day bill auction on November 19.
Banks will pay 51.5 trillion lira to the Treasury for the auction on Wednesday, in return for 164.5 trillion lira to be cashed in from maturing t-bills.
"Auction results were positive. The central bank will probably act tomorrow to drain surplus cash and keep the dollar's rise under control," said Murat Iman from Ata securities.

"The market may drift sideways for a while. Players switch to private sector shares from largely state-owned ones. Activity spills over to the whole market although volume falls which is healthy," he said.
Brokers said year-end profit prospects of companies began to fuel selective demand, but higher volume was needed for the market to advance towards its $1 index target.
